# Static Memory Model

TinyBFT reserves all in-flight protocol message storage at compile
time. Three statically-allocated region structs are embedded by value
inside `tbft_replica_t` — `ar` (agreement), `cr` (checkpoint), and
`sr` (special) — and the steady-state hot path performs no heap
allocation. This document covers what each region stores, how it is
indexed, when it is garbage-collected, and how to size it for a given
cluster.

## Overview

The fundamental design decision: every in-flight PBFT message lives
inside a fixed-size buffer that is part of `tbft_replica_t`. The
message types that the system tracks are:

- **Hot path (HMAC-authenticated)**: Pre_prepare, Prepare, Commit,
  Checkpoint.
- **Slow path (RSA-signed)**: Request, Reply, View_change,
  New_view, View_change_ack, New_key, Fetch, Meta_data, Data,
  Query_stable, Reply_stable, Fill_request, Status.

The hot path uses the **agreement region** and the **checkpoint
region**. The slow path uses the **special region**. State-transfer
messages (Fetch, Meta_data, Data) flow directly through the transport
and are not retained.

All three regions expose `*_init`, `*_store`, `*_load`, and a
`*_truncate` family of functions. There is no `free` — freed slots
are simply zeroed and the region advances its head pointer.

## Why static allocation matters on ESP32-C3

The ESP32-C3 has roughly 400 KB of total DRAM, of which only ~80 KB
remains free after the WiFi, lwIP, FreeRTOS, and ESP-IDF stacks are
loaded. Fragmenting that heap with many small `malloc` calls
(a) defeats the prefetcher, (b) introduces unbounded worst-case
allocation latency, and (c) makes it impossible to reason about peak
DRAM use at design time.

By sizing all message buffers at compile time from Kconfig values
(`tbft_config.h:12-78`) and embedding them by value in `tbft_replica_t`
(`tbft_replica.h:91-93`), the entire BFT state machine fits in one
statically-allocated object whose size is known at link time. The
host application can place it in any linker section (DRAM, IRAM,
PSRAM) by controlling the allocation site — usually a `static
tbft_replica_t g_replica;` at file scope inside the application
translation unit.

| Region | File | Contents | Scaled by |

| `cr` (checkpoint) | `tbft_checkpoint_region.h:43` | `slots[TBFT_NUM_CKPT_SLOTS]` and `above_window[TBFT_MAX_NUM_REPLICAS]`; each slot holds one Checkpoint per replica | `MAX_NUM_REPLICAS² × CKPT_MSG_SIZE` |
| `sr` (special) | `tbft_special_region.h:34` | View_change (`MAX_NUM_REPLICAS` slots), View_change_ack (`MAX_NUM_REPLICAS²` slots), New_view, New_key, Request cache (`MAX_NUM_CLIENTS`), Reply cache (`MAX_NUM_CLIENTS`) | `MAX_NUM_REPLICAS × MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE` + `MAX_NUM_REPLICAS²` ack slots |

## Agreement region (`tbft_agreement_region_t`)

Holds all in-flight Pre_prepare / Prepare / Commit messages for
sequence numbers inside the current window.

### Struct layout

```text
tbft_agreement_region_t   (tbft_agreement_region.h:30-37)
+--------------------------------------------+
| slices[TBFT_WINDOW_SIZE]                  |  <- circular buffer
|     each slice:                            |
|     +----------------------------------+   |
|     | tbft_prepared_cert_t            |   |
|     |   pp_buf[TBFT_PP_MAX_SIZE]      |   |
|     |   pp_len                       |   |
|     |   tbft_prepare_cert_t pc        |   |
|     |   int64 t_sent_us              |   |
|     |   int32 prepare_threshold      |   |
|     +----------------------------------+   |
|     | tbft_commit_cert_t              |   |
|     |   bmap                          |   |
|     |   val_digests[TBFT_CERT_MAX_VALS]   |
|     |   vals[TBFT_CERT_MAX_VALS]      |   |
|     |     [TBFT_CERT_COMMIT_MSG_SIZE] |   |
|     |   correct[TBFT_CERT_MAX_VALS]   |   |
|     |   num_vals, mym_idx, threshold  |   |
|     +----------------------------------+   |
|     | int64 commit_sent_us            |   |
|     | int64 fill_sent_us              |   |
+--------------------------------------------+
| tbft_seqno_t head                          |  <- lowest live seqno
| int          head_idx                      |  <- circular idx for head
| int          mask = WINDOW_SIZE - 1        |
| int          prepare_threshold (2f)        |
| int          commit_threshold  (2f+1)      |
+--------------------------------------------+
```

The `TBFT_CERT_COMMIT_MSG_SIZE` constant is
`sizeof(tbft_commit_rep_t) + TBFT_AUTH_SIZE` (`tbft_certificate.h:28-29`).
The `TBFT_CERT_MAX_VALS` constant is `f+1` (`tbft_config.h:101`).

### Indexing formula

For sequence number `n` in the window, the slot is:

```c
idx = (ar->head_idx + (n - ar->head)) & ar->mask
```

The implementation is inlined at `tbft_agreement_region.h:70-75`
(`tbft_ar_slice`) and the range guard at lines 60-64
(`tbft_ar_in_range`):

```c
static inline bool tbft_ar_in_range(const tbft_agreement_region_t *ar,
                                    tbft_seqno_t n)
{
    return (n >= ar->head) && (n < ar->head + TBFT_WINDOW_SIZE);
}
```

### Sliding-window diagram

```text
ar->head = 5,  TBFT_WINDOW_SIZE = 4
mask = 0b11 (3)

logical view (seqno):    ... 4   5   6   7   8   9  10  11 ...
                              ^head
                              [   window   ]
                              [5, 6, 7, 8]

storage (slices[4]):   slices[0]  slices[1]  slices[2]  slices[3]
                       seqno=5    seqno=6    seqno=7    seqno=8
                       head_idx=0

next seqno 9 arrives:

logical view:                  ... 4   5   6   7   8   9  10 ...
                                    ^head
                                    [   window     ]
                                    [5, 6, 7, 8, 9]

after wrap:
                       slices[0]  slices[1]  slices[2]  slices[3]
                       seqno=9    seqno=6    seqno=7    seqno=8
                       ^head_idx=0  (overwrote slot 0)
```

Wrap is a single bitmask AND on `head_idx`. Every slice stays at the
same array offset for the entire lifetime of the replica; only the
`head` / `head_idx` / contents cycle.

### Truncation: `tbft_ar_truncate`

When a stable checkpoint advances `last_stable` to `new_head`, the
replica calls `tbft_ar_truncate(ar, new_head)`
(`tbft_agreement_region.c:118-146`):

1. Compute `full_delta = new_head - ar->head` (full jump, not capped).
2. Compute `delta = min(full_delta, TBFT_WINDOW_SIZE)` (capped for the
   per-slot clear loop, to avoid iterating billions of times on a
   large fetch jump — comment at lines 125-127).
3. Clear up to `WINDOW_SIZE` slots starting at `head_idx`:
   - `tbft_prepared_cert_clear` on each `prepared_cert`
   - `tbft_commit_cert_clear` on each `commit_cert`
   - Reset `commit_sent_us` and `fill_sent_us` to 0.
4. Advance the circular pointer by the **full** jump:
   `ar->head_idx = (ar->head_idx + full_delta) & mask` —
   not the capped delta. Comment at lines 138-143 explains: using the
   capped delta here would leave `head` far behind `new_head` when
   `full_delta > WINDOW_SIZE`, permanently rejecting all consensus
   messages via `tbft_ar_in_range`.
5. Set `ar->head = new_head`.

### Memory math (f=1, n=4, WINDOW=4, MAX_MESSAGE=2048)

Constants:

- `TBFT_PP_MAX_SIZE = TBFT_MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE = 2048`
- `TBFT_CERT_MAX_VALS = f+1 = 2`
- `TBFT_CERT_COMMIT_MSG_SIZE = sizeof(tbft_commit_rep_t) + TBFT_AUTH_SIZE`
  - `tbft_commit_rep_t` = 16 (hdr) + 8 (view) + 8 (seqno) + 32 (digest) + 4 (id) + 4 (pad) = 72 bytes
  - `TBFT_AUTH_SIZE = TBFT_HMAC_SIZE * (TBFT_MAX_NUM_REPLICAS - 1) = 32 * 3 = 96` bytes
  - → 168 bytes per commit slot
- `TBFT_CERT_PREPARE_MSG_SIZE = 72 + 96 = 168` bytes (same shape as commit)
- `tbft_prepared_cert_t` = 2048 (pp_buf) + 4 (pp_len) + 168 (pc.vals) + 32 (pc.val_digests) + 8 (pc.bmap) + 8 (pc.correct) + 8 (num_vals+mym_idx+threshold padding) + 8 (t_sent_us) ≈ 2300 bytes
- `tbft_commit_cert_t` = 168 × 2 (vals) + 32 × 2 (val_digests) + 8 (bmap) + 8 (correct×2) + 12 (num_vals+mym_idx+threshold) ≈ 440 bytes
- slice = 2300 + 440 + 16 (commit_sent_us+fill_sent_us) ≈ 2756 bytes
- region = 4 × 2756 + 24 (head+head_idx+mask+2 thresholds) ≈ **11,048 bytes ≈ 11 KB**

This is the dominant region. The `memcalc.sh` script in
`examples/counter/` automates the same calculation with real
compile-time sizes.

## Checkpoint region (`tbft_checkpoint_region_t`)

Holds Checkpoint messages from each replica at each seqno, plus a
small above-window side buffer for checkpoints that originate from
replicas ahead of the local window.

### `slots[]`

`tbft_checkpoint_region.h:44` declares
`tbft_ckpt_slot_t slots[TBFT_NUM_CKPT_SLOTS]`. The number of slots is
`WINDOW_SIZE / CHECKPOINT_INTERVAL + 2` (`tbft_config.h:95`).
Indexing: `(seqno / CHECKPOINT_INTERVAL) % NUM_CKPT_SLOTS`
(`tbft_checkpoint_region.c:4-10`).

```text
tbft_ckpt_slot_t   (tbft_checkpoint_region.h:23-40)
+------------------------------------------+
| tbft_seqno_t seqno   (alias guard)        |
| uint8_t msgs[TBFT_MAX_NUM_REPLICAS]       |
|           [TBFT_CKPT_MSG_SIZE]            |
| int      msg_lens[TBFT_MAX_NUM_REPLICAS]  |
| bool     present[TBFT_MAX_NUM_REPLICAS]   |
| int      n_candidates                     |
| tbft_digest_t cand_digests[TBFT_CERT_MAX_VALS] |
| int      cand_counts[TBFT_CERT_MAX_VALS]  |
| int      match_count                      |
| tbft_digest_t winning_digest              |
+------------------------------------------+
```

`TBFT_CKPT_MSG_SIZE = sizeof(tbft_checkpoint_rep_t) + TBFT_AUTH_SIZE`
(`tbft_checkpoint_region.h:20`). With f=1, n=4:
- `tbft_checkpoint_rep_t` = 16 (hdr) + 8 (seqno) + 32 (digest) + 4 (id) + 4 (pad) = 64 bytes
- `TBFT_AUTH_SIZE = 96` (as above)
- → 160 bytes per Checkpoint message

A single slot for f=1, n=4, with `MAX_NUM_REPLICAS=4`:

- 4 × 160 = 640 bytes of `msgs`
- 4 × 4 = 16 bytes `msg_lens`
- 4 bytes `present`
- 8 + 64 (2 × digest) + 8 (2 × count) = 80 bytes candidates
- 4 + 32 = 36 bytes match tracking
- 8 bytes `seqno`
- ≈ **784 bytes per slot**

With `WINDOW_SIZE=4`, `CHECKPOINT_INTERVAL=2`:
`NUM_CKPT_SLOTS = 4/2 + 2 = 4` slots → 4 × 784 ≈ **3,136 bytes**.

### `above_window[]`

`tbft_ckpt_slot_t above_window[TBFT_MAX_NUM_REPLICAS]`
(`tbft_checkpoint_region.h:45`). One slot per replica, each
holding at most one above-window Checkpoint. With f=1, n=4:
4 × 784 ≈ **3,136 bytes**. Total `cr` ≈ **6,272 bytes**.

### Stability logic

`tbft_cr_store` (`tbft_checkpoint_region.c:20-84`) is the write path.
It uses **multi-candidate digest tracking** to defend against a
Byzantine replica that arrives first and tries to set
`winning_digest` to a bogus value:

1. Find the candidate index `ci` matching the incoming digest
   (line 56-61). If absent and there is room, register a new candidate
   (`n_candidates < TBFT_CERT_MAX_VALS`); otherwise refuse the message
   (line 67-73) because with more than `TBFT_CERT_MAX_VALS` distinct
   values no quorum is reachable (pigeonhole).
2. Increment `cand_counts[ci]`.
3. If `cand_counts[ci] > match_count`, promote that candidate to
   `winning_digest` (lines 78-81).
4. Return `match_count >= cr->threshold` (the caller's "stable" signal).

Slot-aliasing guard (lines 38-41): if the slot's `seqno` field
doesn't match the incoming seqno, the slot is from a previous window
cycle — `memset` it before storing. Without this, stale votes from an
old checkpoint can spuriously complete a quorum at the new seqno.

Above-window storage is at `tbft_checkpoint_region.c:120-149` and is
write-once-monotone: an incoming message is rejected unless its seqno
is strictly greater than what is already stored. Comment at
lines 144-148 notes that `match_count` is set to 1 only as a
placeholder for `tbft_cr_load`'s `present[0]` check — above-window
entries do NOT contribute to quorum detection and `tbft_cr_count`
must not be called for them.

`tbft_cr_truncate` (`tbft_checkpoint_region.c:168-185`) clears any
slot whose `seqno <= stable_seqno` in both `slots[]` and
`above_window[]`.

## Special region (`tbft_special_region_t`)

Holds all non-hot-path protocol messages. The struct is at
`tbft_special_region.h:34-56`.

### `TBFT_SR_SLOT` macro

```c
#define TBFT_SR_SLOT(max_size)  \
    struct { uint8_t buf[(max_size)]; int len; bool valid; }
```

(`tbft_special_region.h:31-32`.) Every storage slot in the special
region is an instance of this anonymous struct, expanded by the
preprocessor into a `{ buffer, length, validity }` triple. `valid`
clears the slot; `len` is the actual byte count of the stored message;
`buf` is the message bytes.

The implementation reuses two helper macros
(`tbft_special_region.c:16-33`):

```c
#define SR_STORE(slot, m, mlen, maxlen)  do { ... return true; } while (0)
#define SR_LOAD(slot, lenout)            do { ... return buf; } while (0)
```

`SR_STORE` rejects negative or oversized `mlen`; `SR_LOAD` returns
`NULL` and zeros `*len_out` if `valid == false`.

### Per-type slot layout

```text
tbft_special_region_t   (tbft_special_region.h:34-56)
+--------------------------------------------------------------+
| TBFT_SR_SLOT(TBFT_VC_MSG_MAX_SIZE)                           |
|   view_change[TBFT_MAX_NUM_REPLICAS]                         |
|     = MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE * MAX_NUM_REPLICAS                    |
+--------------------------------------------------------------+
| TBFT_SR_SLOT(sizeof(tbft_vc_ack_rep_t))                       |
|   vc_ack[TBFT_MAX_NUM_REPLICAS][TBFT_MAX_NUM_REPLICAS]        |
|     = sizeof(vc_ack) * MAX_NUM_REPLICAS^2                    |
+--------------------------------------------------------------+
| TBFT_SR_SLOT(TBFT_NV_MSG_MAX_SIZE)  new_view                 |
|     = MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE                                       |
+--------------------------------------------------------------+
| TBFT_SR_SLOT(TBFT_NK_MSG_MAX_SIZE)  new_key                  |
|     = sizeof(new_key_rep) + MAX_NUM_REPLICAS * sizeof(slot)  |
|       = 24 + MAX_NUM_REPLICAS * 260                          |
+--------------------------------------------------------------+
| TBFT_SR_SLOT(TBFT_REQ_MSG_MAX_SIZE)                          |
|   request[TBFT_MAX_NUM_CLIENTS]                              |
|     = MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE * MAX_NUM_CLIENTS                     |
+--------------------------------------------------------------+
| TBFT_SR_SLOT(TBFT_REP_MSG_MAX_SIZE)                          |
|   reply[TBFT_MAX_NUM_CLIENTS]                                |
|     = (sizeof(reply_rep) + MAX_REPLY_SIZE + SIG_SIZE)        |
|       * MAX_NUM_CLIENTS                                      |
+--------------------------------------------------------------+
| int num_replicas                                             |
| int num_clients                                              |
+--------------------------------------------------------------+
```

The size bounds are defined at `tbft_special_region.h:22-28`:

| Macro | Definition |
|-------|-----------|
| `TBFT_VC_MSG_MAX_SIZE` | `TBFT_MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE` |
| `TBFT_NV_MSG_MAX_SIZE` | `TBFT_MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE` |
| `TBFT_NK_MSG_MAX_SIZE` | `sizeof(tbft_new_key_rep_t) + TBFT_MAX_NUM_REPLICAS * sizeof(tbft_new_key_slot_t)` |
| `TBFT_REQ_MSG_MAX_SIZE` | `TBFT_MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE` |
| `TBFT_REP_MSG_MAX_SIZE` | `sizeof(tbft_reply_rep_t) + TBFT_MAX_REPLY_SIZE + TBFT_SIG_SIZE` |

### `New_key` constrains `MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE`

A `New_key` message embeds `(n-1)` RSA-encrypted HMAC session keys
(`tbft_new_key_slot_t` per recipient) plus an RSA signature:

```text
New_key_bytes = sizeof(tbft_new_key_rep_t)               // 24
              + (n - 1) * sizeof(tbft_new_key_slot_t)    // 260 each
              + TBFT_SIG_SIZE                            // 256
```

For `n=4`: 24 + 3*260 + 256 = **1064 bytes**.
For `n=7`: 24 + 6*260 + 256 = **1840 bytes**.

`out_buf` is sized to `TBFT_MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE`
(`tbft_replica.h:120`). A project that raises `MAX_NUM_REPLICAS` and
forgets to raise `MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE` is caught at build time by the
`_Static_assert` chain in `tbft_config.h:133-140` and the reply-size
assertion in `tbft_message.h:75-77`.

### Memory math (f=1, n=4, WINDOW=4, MAX_MESSAGE=2048, MAX_REPLY=512, MAX_CLIENTS=1)

- `view_change`: 4 × 2048 = **8192 bytes**
- `vc_ack`: `sizeof(tbft_vc_ack_rep_t)` = 16+8+4+4 = 32; 4×4 × 32 = **512 bytes**
- `new_view`: **2048 bytes**
- `new_key`: 24 + 4 × (4 + 256) = **1072 bytes**
- `request`: 1 × 2048 = **2048 bytes**
- `reply`: 1 × (32 + 512 + 256) = **800 bytes**
- overhead: 8 bytes for `num_replicas` + `num_clients`
- total `sr` ≈ **14,680 bytes ≈ 14 KB**

## Request queues (`rqueue`, `ro_rqueue`)

`tbft_replica_t` carries two circular FIFOs for incoming client
requests, one for read-write and one for read-only
(`tbft_replica.h:87-88`).

```text
tbft_rqueue_t   (tbft_replica.h:36-41)
+-----------------------------------+
| entries[TBFT_RQUEUE_MAX]          |
|   each:                           |
|     uint8_t buf[TBFT_MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE]  |
|     int     len                    |
|     bool    ro                     |
|     bool    used                   |
+-----------------------------------+
| int head                           |
| int tail                           |
| int count                          |
+-----------------------------------+
```

With `RQUEUE_MAX=4`, `MAX_MESSAGE=2048`:
2 × 4 × (2048 + 8 + 2 + 2 + 4 padding) ≈ **16,512 bytes ≈ 16 KB**
per replica. `examples/counter/sdkconfig.defaults` uses
`RQUEUE_MAX=4`; `examples/simple_wallet/sdkconfig.defaults` uses
`RQUEUE_MAX=4` too — both keep this region under DRAM pressure on the
ESP32-C3.

## Buffers (`ndet_buf`, `out_buf`)

`ndet_buf[TBFT_NDET_BUF_SIZE]` (`tbft_replica.h:117`) holds the
non-deterministic-choices payload produced by the primary's
`comp_ndet_cb`. Staging happens here before being copied into the
Pre_prepare. Default `TBFT_NDET_BUF_SIZE = 256` bytes
(`tbft_config.h:48-50`).

`out_buf[TBFT_MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE]` (`tbft_replica.h:120`) is the
outgoing message build buffer. Every message the replica sends
(Pre_prepare, Commit, View_change, New_key, Fill_request, etc.) is
assembled here before being handed to `tbft_node_send`. With
`MAX_MESSAGE=2048`, this is **2 KB**.

Both buffers live directly inside `tbft_replica_t`, not behind
pointers — they migrate with the replica struct.

| `stimer` | `tbft_replica.h:103` | `tbft_itimer_t` | ≈ 16 bytes | Status broadcast |
| `vtimer_period_us` | `tbft_replica.h:107` | `int64_t` | 8 | |
| `stimer_period_us` | `tbft_replica.h:108` | `int64_t` | 8 | |
| `exec_cb` | `tbft_replica.h:111` | `tbft_exec_cb_t` | 4 (fn-ptr) | |
| `comp_ndet_cb` | `tbft_replica.h:112` | `tbft_comp_ndet_cb_t` | 4 (fn-ptr) | |
| `recv_reply_cb` | `tbft_replica.h:113` | `tbft_recv_reply_cb_t` | 4 (fn-ptr) | |
| `ndet_max_len` | `tbft_replica.h:114` | `int` | 4 | |
| `ndet_buf[]` | `tbft_replica.h:117` | `uint8_t[NDET]` | `TBFT_NDET_BUF_SIZE` | Default 256 |
| `out_buf[]` | `tbft_replica.h:120` | `uint8_t[MAX_MSG]` | `TBFT_MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE` | Default 2048 |
| `running` | `tbft_replica.h:123` | `volatile bool` | 4 | |
| `yield_counter` | `tbft_replica.h:129` | `int` | 4 | |
| `consecutive_mac_failures` | `tbft_replica.h:135` | `int` | 4 | |
| `view_installed_us` | `tbft_replica.h:140` | `int64_t` | 8 | |
| `view_start_executed` | `tbft_replica.h:146` | `int64_t` | 8 | |
| `evt_group` | `tbft_replica.h:149` | `EventGroupHandle_t` | 4 (ptr) | |

`tbft_node_t` (`tbft_node.h:22-50`) is roughly:

| Field | Type | Approx. size |
|-------|------|--------------|
| `node_id`, `max_faulty`, `num_replicas`, `threshold`, `view`, `cur_primary` | mixed scalars | ≈ 32 |
| `principals[N+clients]` | `tbft_principal_t *[N+clients]` | 4 × (R+C) |
| `num_principals` | `int` | 4 |
| `local_principal` | `tbft_principal_t *` | 4 |
| `transport` | `tbft_transport_t *` | 4 |
| `recv_buf[]` | `uint8_t[MAX_MSG]` | 2048 |
| `atimer` | `tbft_itimer_t` | 16 |
| `auth_timeout_us` | `int64_t` | 8 |
| `rid_counter` | `uint64_t` | 8 |

Approximate total for f=1, n=4, MAX_REPLICAS=4, MAX_CLIENTS=1, RQUEUE=4, MAX_MESSAGE=2048:

| Subtotal | Bytes |
|----------|-------|
| `node` (excluding principals array) | ≈ 2,140 |
| `principals` array | 4 × 5 × 4 = 80 |
| sequence-number scalars | ≈ 88 |
| `last_*_rid` arrays | 8 × 3 × 5 = 120 |
| `rqueue` + `ro_rqueue` | ≈ 16,512 |
| `ar` | ≈ 11,048 |
| `cr` | ≈ 6,272 |
| `sr` | ≈ 14,680 |
| `state` | (host) |
| `vi` + timers + scalars | ≈ 80 |
| `ndet_buf` | 256 |
| `out_buf` | 2048 |
| **subtotal without `state`** | **≈ 53,300 bytes ≈ 52 KB** |

This fits comfortably in the ESP32-C3's free heap after the WiFi
stack (~80 KB free) when `state` is a small application buffer. For
larger deployments (`n=7`, `MAX_MESSAGE=2048`), the `ar` and `sr`
regions scale roughly linearly and the `cr` region scales as `n²` —
use `examples/counter/memcalc.sh` for an exact build-time
calculation.
